# Experiment Design — BAdam vs LoRA on Zero-Shot Math for Llama-3-70B

> **Design-only document. No training, evaluation, or experimentation was executed.** The sandbox has no GPU, no network, and no ML packages; every runtime figure below is a reasoned estimate to be validated on an external cluster.

---

## 1) Rationale

**Reframed research question (single IV).** Holding the base model, training data, optimizer recipe, and evaluation harness fixed, does the *adaptation method* change zero-shot math performance? Conditions:
- **A — LoRA (control):** freeze pretrained weights; train low-rank adapters ΔW = BA on attention matrices (q,k,v,o; rank r, α, dropout) with AdamW.
- **B — BAdam (treatment):** full-parameter block-coordinate optimization — parameters partitioned into blocks; per step one block is updated with Adam while the rest stay frozen at pretrained values; optimizer state is kept only for the active block (block size ≈ 1/12 of all parameters; data-dependent update scheme, anchored to the official BAdam repo before locking).

**Why the comparison is meaningful.** LoRA restricts updates to a low-rank subspace of attention weights (a few % of parameters, expressively constrained), which is cheap but may under-fit. BAdam updates *all* parameters at full rank while keeping memory near LoRA by serializing optimizer state across blocks. The scientific question is whether the extra full-rank expressiveness (via blockwise Adam) translates to better *zero-shot generalization* on held-out math reasoning — i.e., whether the low-rank bottleneck, not the optimizer, is the limiting factor. This is exactly the trade-off the BAdam paper claims to invert (full-rank quality at PEFT-like memory), and it is worth re-testing at the much larger Llama-3-70B scale and on zero-shot (not in-distribution few-shot) evaluation.

**Directional hypothesis (pre-registered).** We expect BAdam ≥ LoRA on zero-shot GSM8K/MATH because full-rank updates are strictly more expressive; the null is that the two are indistinguishable given the matched budget.

---

## 2) Controls — matched-control recipe

Everything below is identical across conditions **except the adaptation method**.

| Controlled factor | Specification |
|---|---|
| Base model | Llama-3-70B **base** (non-instruct), pinned HF revision, commit hash + parameter hash recorded |
| Training data | MathInstruct, full 261K pairs, canonical seeded shuffling; Alpaca-style template (MAmmoTH) identical for both conditions |
| Data split | Random 95/5 train / held-out selection split (seed 0), **same split for both conditions**; selection split used ONLY for checkpoint selection, never for benchmark conclusion |
| Optimizer | Adam family, β1=0.9, β2=0.999, ε=1e-8, weight decay 0 (neutral for both); bf16 compute, fp32 master copy of active parameters only |
| LR schedule | Cosine decay to 10% of peak; warmup = 3% of total steps; **base matched peak LR = 1e-4** (per-method LR sensitivity arm, below) |
| Batch | LoRA: global batch 64 examples (=8192 tokens) via gradient accumulation. BAdam: one data shard per block-step (≈261K/12 ≈ 21.7K examples) split into the *same micro-batch size* as LoRA (64) with internal accumulation — the only structural difference is the larger effective batch size per optimizer step |
| Sequence length | 1024 tokens, identical truncation policy |
| Training length | **3 full data exposures** (definition below) |
| Mixed precision | bf16 throughout, gradient checkpointing on, identical |
| Seeds | seeds {0,1,2} shared across conditions (same data order, dropout, LoRA init, BAdam block permutation); 3 seeds per condition primary |
| Selection metric | Zero-shot exact match on held-out selection split under the same prompt as benchmarks |
| Eval decoding | Greedy (T=0, top_p=1), max_new_tokens 512, same tokenizer |
| Eval pipeline | Same zero-shot prompt, same answer-extraction + scoring code, run blinded to method |

### Fair exposure — explicit resolution
The structural difference is that **data-dependent BAdam** partitions data into as many shards as parameter blocks, and block *i* is updated only on shard *i*; LoRA's every parameter sees every example each epoch.

**Choice:** define *data exposure* as **the number of times each individual example is presented to the (whole) parameter space**, and set **3 exposures for both conditions** — i.e., LoRA trains for 3 epochs; BAdam runs 3 rounds, where one round = one pass through the full dataset with block i seeing shard i exactly once. After 3 exposures every example has contributed to updates 3 times under both methods, which is the only comparison that is fair by construction. This also matches the BAdam paper's MathInstruct setting (3 epochs, Llama2 scale), which we replicate in spirit.

**Consequence & mitigation.** Equal exposure still leaves two structural mismatches: (i) BAdam's per-step effective batch (≈21.7K examples) is much larger than LoRA's 64-example global batch; large batches generally want higher LR. This is *inherent* to the data-dependent scheme and should not be force-normalized (that would distort each method). We therefore: (a) run the **LR-sensitivity arm** below so neither method is handicapped by a shared LR; and (b) add a **robustness arm** using the *data-independent (cyclical)* BAdam variant, in which per-step batch size and steps-per-exposure match LoRA exactly — if the primary conclusion reproduces in this arm, it is robust to shard-batch/LR interaction. The data-dependent scheme remains the primary arm because it is the paper's flagship, memory-efficient scheme.

**Data leakage check (design-time).** MathInstruct samples *training* splits of source datasets; benchmarks use held-out *test* splits (GSM8K official 1319; MATH official 5000). We will verify by n-gram overlap that no benchmark test item appears in the training/selection split; if any overlap is found, those items are excluded from the benchmark and documented.

### LR-sensitivity arm (tuning is on 1 seed only)
For each method, run an LR scan {5e-5, 1e-4, 2e-4} on **one seed**, select each method's best peak LR by held-out selection-split accuracy, then run the **3-seed primary comparison at each method's chosen LR**. This answers "is the matched-LR comparison a fair test of the methods" and isolates method-vs-tuning effects. The 3-seed comparison is the only conclusion-bearing result; scan runs are diagnostic.

---

## 3) Analysis plan (pre-registered)

**Primary metric:** zero-shot exact-match accuracy on **GSM8K** (1319 items). MATH (5000) is a primary supporting co-benchmark; AQuA, SVAMP, ASDiv, TheoremQA are supporting (if budget permits) for breadth.

**Aggregation.** Per seed s and method m: selected-checkpoint accuracy a(m,s). Report mean±SE over 3 seeds, plus the paired seed-wise differences d_s = a(BAdam,s) − a(LoRA,s) (paired because identical splits/seeds are reused).

**Decision rule — "BAdam better" iff** (i) d_s > 0 for **all three** seeds (sign consistency), **and** (ii) the 95% confidence interval of the difference excludes 0, where the CI is computed two ways: (a) **per-item bootstrap** (10,000 resamples of the 1319 GSM8K items within each run, giving a bootstrap distribution of the accuracy difference for the representative run) and (b) a paired t-test/Studentized bootstrap over the 3 seed-wise deltas. Both must exclude 0.
- **Inconclusive:** CI contains 0, or seed signs are mixed, or the point estimate of the difference is < 1 pp. Also pre-registered: *BAdam not better* (i.e., d ≤ 0 or not distinguishable) is a valid, informative answer to the research question; the experiment is not designed to force a positive result.
- **Effect-size guardrail:** with n=3 seeds and GSM8K SE ≈ 1.4 pp per run, only effects ≳ 2–4 pp are reliably detectable at 70B cost; this limitation is stated in the report.

**Reporting requirements.** (1) Per-benchmark table: mean±SE and 95% CI for both methods on GSM8K, MATH, and any supporting benchmarks. (2) Per-MATH-subject breakdown (7 subjects). (3) Training/selection curves (val accuracy vs exposure) for every run — transparent evidence that nothing is selected on benchmark peeking. (4) Exact LR used per method, chosen checkpoint index, and full decoding/parsing settings. (5) All reported numbers come with the seed list, so the analysis is fully reproducible.

---

## 4) Feasibility (external cluster; estimates only)

**Memory.** Llama-3-70B in bf16 = **~140 GB**, requiring ≥4×80GB just for weights; plan **8× H100-80GB** (or 16× A100-80GB) with FSDP/DeepSpeed-ZeRO sharding + activation checkpointing.
- **LoRA:** adapters (rank 16, 4 targets, 80 layers) ≈ a few hundred M params → adapter grads + Adam states ≈ a few GB. Memory is dominated by model weights + activations. Comfortably fits in 8×80GB.
- **BAdam:** full forward/backward (activation checkpointing recompute); optimizer state only for the **active block** = 1/12 × 70B ≈ 5.8B params → fp32 Adam m,v ≈ 46GB + active-block grads ≈ 12GB + optional fp32 master ≈ 23GB ⇒ per-block working set ≈ 50–80GB, mapped to the shards hosting that block; frozen weights stay bf16 (possibly offloaded). Feasible on 8×80GB but the tightest constraint — validated in the pilot.

**Wall clock (rough).** MathInstruct ≈ 261K pairs ≈ ~65M tokens.
- LoRA: ~2–4 h/exposure on 8×H100 (FSDP + checkpointing overhead) ⇒ ~6–12 h for 3 exposures.
- BAdam: full-model forward/backward per token (no adapter shortcut) ≈ 4–10 h/exposure ⇒ ~12–30 h for 3 rounds. Expect BAdam ≈ 1.5–2.5× LoRA cost; total primary budget (1-seed LR scan for 2 methods + 3-seed primary for 2 methods + robustness arm + evals) ≈ **1.5–3 weeks** on 8×H100. These are order-of-magnitude planning figures, to be replaced by measured throughput after the pilot.

**Checkpoint/resume.** Save full (model + optimizer + data-order state) sharded checkpoints every exposure (and mid-exposure) for resume-capable training; LoRA saves adapter + frozen-ref; BAdam saves per-block optimizer state. Selection-split eval runs at every checkpoint; benchmark eval only on the selected checkpoint. Benchmarks evaluate greedily in one forward pass — negligible cost vs training.

**Recommended pilot (before full runs).** (1) *Smoke:* one BAdam step + one LoRA step on the real 70B job to validate the official BAdam implementation's Llama-3-70B support, block partitioning (GQA/RoPE layers), memory ceiling, and throughput. (2) *Scale pilot:* identical recipe on **Llama-3-8B** with the same data/splits/prompts to validate the statistical pipeline, the LR scan, the parser, and the decision rule cheaply (transferred tentatively). (3) *Verification:* confirm BAdam repo's MathInstruct block size / LR / epochs before freezing hyperparameters.

---

## 5) Assumptions vs uncertainties

| # | Item | Status |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | External cluster 8–16×80GB (H100/A100-class), ~1.5–3 weeks wall clock | **Assumption / design choice** (not verifiable here) |
| A2 | BAdam = data-dependent scheme, block 1/12, LR 1e-4 base, 3 exposures | **Assumption**, to be anchored to official repo/paper |
| A3 | LoRA: rank 16, α=2r, dropout 0.05, targets q,k,v,o, LR 1e-4 | **Assumption / design choice** (common 70B PEFT practice) |
| A4 | Equal data exposure = 3 presentations per example (explicit definition above) | **Design choice** (stated rationale) |
| A5 | Matched base LR + LR-sensitivity arm; 3 seeds primary | **Design choice** |
| A6 | Zero-shot pipeline: greedy decoding, fixed CoT prompt, shared parser, selection split only | **Design choice** |
| A7 | Decision rule (all-seed sign consistency + bootstrap CI excluding 0); inconclusive thresholds | **Design choice / pre-registered** |
| U1 | Exact BAdam hyperparameters/details from the paper (block size, LR, epochs on MathInstruct) | **To be verified externally** (no network; not in workspace) |
| U2 | Official BAdam code correctness + memory at 70B (GQA, block partition, distributed shards) | **To be verified** in pilot/smoke test |
| U3 | Per-step batch/LR interaction in data-dependent scheme (structural, not force-normalized) | **To be assessed** via LR arm + cyclical robustness arm |
| U4 | Zero-shot prompt sensitivity & parser edge cases | **To be assessed** via alternate-prompt check + parser validation |
| U5 | Wall-clock/memory estimates above | **Estimates; measured in pilot** |
| U6 | Effect size at 70B (detectable ≥2–4 pp at n=3) | **Statistical limitation, stated in report** |

**Bottom line:** this design gives a pre-registered, statistically grounded answer to "does BAdam beat LoRA on zero-shot math for Llama-3-70B finetuned on MathInstruct," with a fair matched-control recipe, an explicit resolution of the equal-exposure problem, a power-aware decision rule, and a feasibility plan with a pilot gate before the expensive runs. No experiment was executed.

## 1) Rationale

**Reframed research question (single IV).** Holding the base model, training data, optimizer recipe, and evaluation harness fixed, does the *adaptation method* change zero-shot math performance? Conditions:
- **A — LoRA (control):** freeze pretrained weights; train low-rank adapters ΔW = BA on attention matrices (q,k,v,o; rank r, α, dropout) with AdamW.
- **B — BAdam (treatment):** full-parameter block-coordinate optimization — parameters partitioned into blocks; per step one block is updated with Adam while the rest stay frozen at pretrained values; optimizer state is kept only for the active block (block size ≈ 1/12 of all parameters; data-dependent update scheme, anchored to the official BAdam repo before locking).

**Why the comparison is meaningful.** LoRA restricts updates to a low-rank subspace of attention weights (a few % of parameters, expressively constrained), which is cheap but may under-fit. BAdam updates *all* parameters at full rank while keeping memory near LoRA by serializing optimizer state across blocks. The scientific question is whether the extra full-rank expressiveness (via blockwise Adam) translates to better *zero-shot generalization* on held-out math reasoning — i.e., whether the low-rank bottleneck, not the optimizer, is the limiting factor. This is exactly the trade-off the BAdam paper claims to invert (full-rank quality at PEFT-like memory), and it is worth re-testing at the much larger Llama-3-70B scale and on zero-shot (not in-distribution few-shot) evaluation.

**Directional hypothesis (pre-registered).** We expect BAdam ≥ LoRA on zero-shot GSM8K/MATH because full-rank updates are strictly more expressive; the null is that the two are indistinguishable given the matched budget.

### Fair exposure — explicit resolution
The structural difference is that **data-dependent BAdam** partitions data into as many shards as parameter blocks, and block *i* is updated only on shard *i*; LoRA's every parameter sees every example each epoch.

**Choice:** define *data exposure* as **the number of times each individual example is presented to the (whole) parameter space**, and set **3 exposures for both conditions** — i.e., LoRA trains for 3 epochs; BAdam runs 3 rounds, where one round = one pass through the full dataset with block i seeing shard i exactly once. After 3 exposures every example has contributed to updates 3 times under both methods, which is the only comparison that is fair by construction. This also matches the BAdam paper's MathInstruct setting (3 epochs, Llama2 scale), which we replicate in spirit.

**Consequence & mitigation.** Equal exposure still leaves two structural mismatches: (i) BAdam's per-step effective batch (≈21.7K examples) is much larger than LoRA's 64-example global batch; large batches generally want higher LR. This is *inherent* to the data-dependent scheme and should not be force-normalized (that would distort each method). We therefore: (a) run the **LR-sensitivity arm** below so neither method is handicapped by a shared LR; and (b) add a **robustness arm** using the *data-independent (cyclical)* BAdam variant, in which per-step batch size and steps-per-exposure match LoRA exactly — if the primary conclusion reproduces in this arm, it is robust to shard-batch/LR interaction. The data-dependent scheme remains the primary arm because it is the paper's flagship, memory-efficient scheme.

**Data leakage check (design-time).** MathInstruct samples *training* splits of source datasets; benchmarks use held-out *test* splits (GSM8K official 1319; MATH official 5000). We will verify by n-gram overlap that no benchmark test item appears in the training/selection split; if any overlap is found, those items are excluded from the benchmark and documented.

### LR-sensitivity arm (tuning is on 1 seed only)
For each method, run an LR scan {5e-5, 1e-4, 2e-4} on **one seed**, select each method's best peak LR by held-out selection-split accuracy, then run the **3-seed primary comparison at each method's chosen LR**. This answers "is the matched-LR comparison a fair test of the methods" and isolates method-vs-tuning effects. The 3-seed comparison is the only conclusion-bearing result; scan runs are diagnostic.

## 3) Analysis plan (pre-registered)

**Primary metric:** zero-shot exact-match accuracy on **GSM8K** (1319 items). MATH (5000) is a primary supporting co-benchmark; AQuA, SVAMP, ASDiv, TheoremQA are supporting (if budget permits) for breadth.

**Aggregation.** Per seed s and method m: selected-checkpoint accuracy a(m,s). Report mean±SE over 3 seeds, plus the paired seed-wise differences d_s = a(BAdam,s) − a(LoRA,s) (paired because identical splits/seeds are reused).

**Decision rule — "BAdam better" iff** (i) d_s > 0 for **all three** seeds (sign consistency), **and** (ii) the 95% confidence interval of the difference excludes 0, where the CI is computed two ways: (a) **per-item bootstrap** (10,000 resamples of the 1319 GSM8K items within each run, giving a bootstrap distribution of the accuracy difference for the representative run) and (b) a paired t-test/Studentized bootstrap over the 3 seed-wise deltas. Both must exclude 0.
- **Inconclusive:** CI contains 0, or seed signs are mixed, or the point estimate of the difference is < 1 pp. Also pre-registered: *BAdam not better* (i.e., d ≤ 0 or not distinguishable) is a valid, informative answer to the research question; the experiment is not designed to force a positive result.
- **Effect-size guardrail:** with n=3 seeds and GSM8K SE ≈ 1.4 pp per run, only effects ≳ 2–4 pp are reliably detectable at 70B cost; this limitation is stated in the report.

**Reporting requirements.** (1) Per-benchmark table: mean±SE and 95% CI for both methods on GSM8K, MATH, and any supporting benchmarks. (2) Per-MATH-subject breakdown (7 subjects). (3) Training/selection curves (val accuracy vs exposure) for every run — transparent evidence that nothing is selected on benchmark peeking. (4) Exact LR used per method, chosen checkpoint index, and full decoding/parsing settings. (5) All reported numbers come with the seed list, so the analysis is fully reproducible.

## 4) Feasibility (external cluster; estimates only)

**Memory.** Llama-3-70B in bf16 = **~140 GB**, requiring ≥4×80GB just for weights; plan **8× H100-80GB** (or 16× A100-80GB) with FSDP/DeepSpeed-ZeRO sharding + activation checkpointing.
- **LoRA:** adapters (rank 16, 4 targets, 80 layers) ≈ a few hundred M params → adapter grads + Adam states ≈ a few GB. Memory is dominated by model weights + activations. Comfortably fits in 8×80GB.
- **BAdam:** full forward/backward (activation checkpointing recompute); optimizer state only for the **active block** = 1/12 × 70B ≈ 5.8B params → fp32 Adam m,v ≈ 46GB + active-block grads ≈ 12GB + optional fp32 master ≈ 23GB ⇒ per-block working set ≈ 50–80GB, mapped to the shards hosting that block; frozen weights stay bf16 (possibly offloaded). Feasible on 8×80GB but the tightest constraint — validated in the pilot.

**Wall clock (rough).** MathInstruct ≈ 261K pairs ≈ ~65M tokens.
- LoRA: ~2–4 h/exposure on 8×H100 (FSDP + checkpointing overhead) ⇒ ~6–12 h for 3 exposures.
- BAdam: full-model forward/backward per token (no adapter shortcut) ≈ 4–10 h/exposure ⇒ ~12–30 h for 3 rounds. Expect BAdam ≈ 1.5–2.5× LoRA cost; total primary budget (1-seed LR scan for 2 methods + 3-seed primary for 2 methods + robustness arm + evals) ≈ **1.5–3 weeks** on 8×H100. These are order-of-magnitude planning figures, to be replaced by measured throughput after the pilot.

**Checkpoint/resume.** Save full (model + optimizer + data-order state) sharded checkpoints every exposure (and mid-exposure) for resume-capable training; LoRA saves adapter + frozen-ref; BAdam saves per-block optimizer state. Selection-split eval runs at every checkpoint; benchmark eval only on the selected checkpoint. Benchmarks evaluate greedily in one forward pass — negligible cost vs training.

**Recommended pilot (before full runs).** (1) *Smoke:* one BAdam step + one LoRA step on the real 70B job to validate the official BAdam implementation's Llama-3-70B support, block partitioning (GQA/RoPE layers), memory ceiling, and throughput. (2) *Scale pilot:* identical recipe on **Llama-3-8B** with the same data/splits/prompts to validate the statistical pipeline, the LR scan, the parser, and the decision rule cheaply (transferred tentatively). (3) *Verification:* confirm BAdam repo's MathInstruct block size / LR / epochs before freezing hyperparameters.
